children: The BSE Sensex crossed the 80,000 mark in intraday trade on Friday, November 6, 2026, reclaiming a key psychological milestone it had last touched on March 5, 2026. The index touched an intraday high of 80,080.59 before trading at 80,027.74, up 717.73 points or 0.90 per cent, against its previous close of 79,310.01. The Nifty 50 rose 161.60 points or 0.66 per cent to 24,698, touching an intraday high of 24,702.60, against a previous close of 24,536.60 and an opening of 24,538.20 at 1.11 pm.

The rally came despite a severe overnight selloff on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq tumbled 5.52 per cent, the S&P 500 fell 4.36 per cent, and the Dow Jones dropped 3.45 per cent, triggered by a broad unwinding of artificial intelligence and semiconductor trades following Democratic gains in the US midterm elections. Asian markets bore the brunt of the fallout, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 plunging approximately 5.9 per cent and South Korea’s Kospi losing over 8.5 per cent, briefly triggering a circuit breaker. SanDisk fell 15 per cent, AMD dropped 12 per cent, and Tesla shed 10 per cent.
Rupee resilience, easing crude, FII inflows give support

India’s relative resilience was underpinned by a firmer rupee, moderating crude oil prices and sustained foreign institutional investor buying. The USD/INR pair was trading around 94.40, extending its decline for a sixth consecutive session, supported by RBI measures to curb speculative activity and a softer US dollar. “A firmer rupee, if sustained, could offer some relief on the imported inflation front,” said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.

WTI crude oil was trading near $92 per barrel, up approximately 0.9 per cent from the previous session, recovering from the $87 region. MCX crude oil opened near ₹8,665 and was trading around ₹8,700, up 1.7 per cent. Brent crude, however, was heading towards its steepest weekly decline since April 2020, as markets assessed prospects of de-escalation in the Middle East. “Geopolitical developments and the possibility of supply disruptions remain important variables,” Ponmudi R noted, adding that US President Donald Trump’s threat to expand military strikes against Iran kept investors on alert.

Among Nifty gainers, Mahindra & Mahindra led with a 3.55 per cent rise to ₹3,238.50, touching a high of ₹3,283.80. Titan climbed 2.52 per cent to ₹4,956.30, with an intraday high of ₹5,003.90. HDFC Bank advanced 2.43 per cent to ₹778.50, while ICICI Bank gained an equal 2.43 per cent to ₹1,536.50. NTPC rose 2.06 per cent to ₹320.15. On the losing side, Shriram Finance fell 2.42 per cent to ₹940.65. Eicher Motors declined 1.76 per cent to ₹7,577.50, Tata Motors (TMPV) dropped 1.67 per cent to ₹288.80, Hindalco shed 1.48 per cent to ₹923.95, and BEL lost 1.35 per cent to ₹389.75.

Information technology stocks bucked the global trend, gaining more than 1 per cent and emerging as early session outperformers, even as their US counterparts were among the hardest hit overnight. Banking and financial stocks provided the broader market its lift, with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank together accounting for significant volume — ₹3,786 crore and ₹3,642 crore respectively.

On the BSE, 3,032 stocks advanced against 1,324 declines, with 187 unchanged, out of 4,543 stocks traded. A total of 117 stocks hit 52-week highs while 60 touched 52-week lows. Upper circuit hits numbered 213 against 152 lower circuit stocks. Nifty 50 advance-decline stood at an equal 25-25 split, reflecting selective buying rather than a broad-based surge.

Precious metals came under pressure. COMEX gold opened with a gap down near $4,100 and was trading around $4,055, down approximately 1.4 per cent, retreating from a two-week high. MCX gold was trading near ₹1,42,150, down approximately 1.35 per cent. COMEX silver fell roughly 1.75 per cent to around $51.50, while MCX silver dropped 1.6 per cent to approximately ₹1,84,200. “The divergence between gold and silver calls for caution. Avoid chasing short-term price moves,” said Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus. Market attention was focused on the US nonfarm payrolls report due later in the day, which could influence Federal Reserve rate expectations and the dollar’s near-term direction.

Technically, the Nifty’s RSI remained in the mid-70s, indicating strong bullish momentum but also suggesting overbought conditions. Immediate resistance was placed at 24,700–24,800, with support at 24,300–24,400. Bank Nifty was facing resistance near the 58,000–58,200 zone, with support at 57,300–57,500. “The domestic technical structure remains strongly bullish, supported by consecutive gains, major trendline breakouts and substantial FII inflows,” said Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking. “Some profit-booking may create intraday volatility, but the broader positive momentum remains intact.”

The Sensex’s return to 80,000 — last seen when it closed at 80,015.90 on March 5 before slipping into an eight-month correction — marked a significant technical milestone for domestic markets, reinforcing what analysts described as a fundamental recovery driven by earnings growth, large-cap valuations and renewed foreign participation. “This ongoing rally has fundamental support from impressive earnings growth which has come better-than-expected,” said Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited. “For financials, tech and auto stocks, there is more upside.”

title: Sensex reclaims 80,000 after March; Nifty tops 24,700 despite global tech rout
